title: Bounded exact controls for the timing-adaptive conversion candidate

renewal.scope: Finite IID controls support the general analytical epoch proof; they do not exhaust adaptive epoch laws.

adaptive_policies.scope: All timing-adaptive query policies in each finite game, with fresh independent copies only after exceptions.

backlog.scope: Necessity of log L order for the generic first-moment counter argument, not a lower bound for all indexes or compilers.

canonical_lookup.scope: Exact finite reduction controls, with no ANN index, timing benchmark, learned encoder or dynamic performance claim.

covering_memory.scope: Known covering-family algebra and dynamic exact-operator controls; bucket oracle is not a balanced-tree benchmark or an implementation of the timed wrapper.

all_prefix_restart.scope: Exact bounded checks of the classical exponential-supermartingale argument; finite games do not prove novelty or replace the all-prefix analytical proof.

covering_spectral.scope: Exact finite controls of the analytical spectral second-moment proof; no numerical eigenvalue approximation or novelty inference.

covering_fingerprints.scope: Finite fingerprints/FHT and complete-function controls, not a production balanced-tree index, benchmark, learned block or claim that compressed tables are independent.

constant_families.scope: Exact parameter arithmetic at an illustrative reset/base cost ratio 4*n, not measured costs or a proof of a practical speedup.

xor_covering.scope: Independent direct sums and exact joint-seed moments support the XOR/direct-bucket proof. Counts are RAM operation identities, not Python performance measurements or a novelty determination.

direct_buckets.scope: Bounded intrusive-list oracle checks deletion handles, raw-key edits, independent payloads and abort cleanup. Selected seeds are correctness controls, not a runtime-distribution experiment or production implementation.

sparse_shell.scope: Exact distributional and Jensen/Rayleigh controls; no sampled keys, numerical eigenvalues, training, performance benchmark or novelty inference. The written proof supplies the uniform theorem.

compact_timing_attack.scope: Exact rational packing/moment controls, exhaustive finite averaging games, a constant-weight geometry, conditional seed distributions and fresh-query cube algebra support the written proofs. Whole-RAM-time classification follows from the written expectation/Markov argument, not an empirical timing experiment. No full-index lower bound, neural model or novelty determination.

full_range_baseline.scope: Exact algebraic boundary checks support the written full-range arithmetic-model baseline derivation. No optimal LSF implementation, Gaussian experiment, finite-word compilation, adaptive-key theorem, measured performance or novelty claim.

sparse_signature_baseline.scope: Exact preallocated-trie oracle checks dynamic admission, atomic rejection, raw verification, scratch cleanup and independent weighted payloads against exhaustive Hamming reads. Integer controls support the written random-shell/asymptotic proof. This is a known signature-dictionary baseline consequence, not a new architecture, optimal implementation, performance benchmark or novelty claim.

product_spectral_baseline.scope: Exact Walsh/tensor algebra and a preallocated-array product decoder checked against direct raw Hamming reads, independent current payloads and full pure-basin perturbation controls. Large-radius boundary cases test correctness, not the subpolynomial regime. This is a classical product-indexing baseline consequence, not a new ML architecture, benchmark or novelty determination.

compound_rebuild_cost.scope: Exact finite controls for the written uniform compound-supermartingale proof. Finite timing games use bounded two-point rebuild marks, with trigger-dependent laws and fresh uniform seeds; actual unbounded geometric trial counts are checked by their closed infinite generating function. No novelty, architecture advantage or exhaustive infinite-adversary computation is claimed.

spectral_mixture_hardness.scope: Exact bounded certificates for an explicit near-identity-kernel encoding of Boolean rectangle means and a raw-bit repetition-basin decoder. All Boolean payload assignments are exhausted for side 2 and 3; larger cases use stated deterministic payload profiles. Every Boolean rectangle query is exhausted for each listed configuration. All raw bit perturbations up to the basin radius are exhausted only for side <=3 and spectral_slack_bits=1. The uniform spectral/retention/reduction proofs are analytical. The OMv conjecture, arbitrary raw-query performance, small-radius hardness, novelty and an architectural advantage are not verified or claimed.

subset_aggregate_candidate.scope: Exact tuple-map algorithm versus independent complete raw Hamming reads. Small dimensions exhaust all raw queries; larger cases exhaust stated one-hot queries for weight 5 and use systematic raw support/bit-flip controls. Dynamic admission is checked against all pair intersections, including proposals outside the initial codebook. Signed cancellations, atomic rejection, deletion/reuse, pure-noise reads, nontrivial independently overwritten/deleted mixtures, spectral row sums and exact parameter bounds are checked. The code is a bounded correctness control, not a finite-word arena implementation, runtime benchmark, learned encoder or novelty/strongest-baseline determination.
